articleTitle: The effectiveness of IoT and machine learning in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Applying the IoT paradigm in agriculture generates an unprecedented amount of data about fields and crops worldwide. With data, machine learning is natural to forecast or estimate crop parameters, which is remarkable for the estimation of evapotranspiration and soil moisture to propose irrigation plans and control, among other applications. This work investigates the literature to evaluate what kind of IoT devices and machine learning algorithms are being applied in precision agriculture and discusses the effectiveness of such equipment and algorithms on different spatial scales. The results indicate IoT devices are commonly applied in small crop areas or greenhouses and for short periods of time, usually less than one growing season. Machine learning models are also applied in similar scenarios, and the effectiveness of such techniques is discussed according to growers' needs and ambitions.

articleTitle: BeeSmart: a real-time remote monitoring and control system for beekeeping
abstract: The development of agriculture has generally come with an increase in the use of agrochemicals and our region is no exception. In consequence, beekeeping production has been negatively affected by the death of bees and product contamination. Besides, the beehive's state of health is a good indicator of the quality of the environment in the area. However, beehives usually are located in remote sites that hamper frequent visits to asses beehive health. Remote monitoring of the production of honey and beehive health would be beneficial for the beekeeping community and also for environmental supervision. This work presents a prototype of a real-time monitoring and control system for apiaries as a first step to providing an integrated solution to beekeepers. The system consists of a device installed in each beehive to measure parameters of interest, such as internal temperature and weight, and transmit this information to a hub connected to the Internet. The internal temperature map is a proxy for the presence and activity of bees. The information collected is presented to beekeepers through a web application where they can access the data of each beehive and open or close its door. Preliminary results show that the proposed approach and system architecture are very promising. Future work includes building a more robust mechanical design, assessing other communication technologies, and a more affordable solution.

articleTitle: Design of a Gateway-based relay node for LoRaWAN multihop networks
abstract: LoRaWAN is one of the protocols responsible for connecting devices to the IoT ecosystem. The protocol provides connectivity with low energy consumption and a large coverage area. However, many scenarios impose difficulties on the transmission, and sometimes it is necessary to increase the coverage using a multihop approach. The objective of this work is to introduce a gateway-based relay device for a multihop LoRaWAN network. The called relay-gateway is an intermediate device capable of receiving data from many sources due to its hardware capabilities. It is reliable in terms of energy consumption because it uses a fixed energy source. The experimental evaluation conducted at the university campus shows that the relay solution is suitable for extending the network and providing connectivity to remote areas. The results show a 50% increase of packet delivery for some places using the relay solution compared with direct transmission using SF7.

articleTitle: Ensuring applications' traffic isolation using IEEE 802.15.4e TSCH through SDWSN slicing
abstract: IEEE 802.15.4e Time Slotted Channel Hopping (TSCH) enables network slicing and brings efficiency to the Software-Defined Wireless Sensor Networks (SDWSNs), which contribute to the Internet of Things (IoT) deployment. However, dealing with the different applications' traffic as a single flow and accommodating them in the same slice could increase the congestion and decrease the Quality of Service (QoS) level. In this paper, the Application Traffic Isolation (ATI) approach is presented. It is implemented using the IT-SDN framework on top of TSCH. The performance evaluation considers up to four applications running simultaneously, comparing the proposed approach to another one that considers the whole applications' traffic as a single flow. Simulation results showed that ATI improved both the delivery rate and delay in the application layer. However, it led to more energy consumption.

articleTitle: Crowded MTC Random Access in NOMA XL-MIMO
abstract: assive MIMO is one of the key technologies to support the growth of massive access attempts by devices, such as in massive machine type communication (mMTC).assive MIMO is one of the key technologies to support the growth of massive access attempts by devices, such as in massive machine type communication (mMTC).M The evolution of antenna array technology brought the recent extra-large scale massive multiple input multiple output (XL-MIMO) systems, seen as a promising technology for providing very high-data rates in high-user density scenarios. Spatial non stationarities and visibility regions (VRs) occur across all huge XL array extension, since its large dimension is of the same order of the distances to the user equipment (UE). We investigate the random access (RA) problem in crowded XL-MIMO scenarios. The proposed non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) visible region extra large array (NVR-XL) protocol takes advantage of the power domain NOMA to allow access of two or more users colliding in the same XL sub-array (SA) selecting the same pilot sequence. The NVR-XL provides a reduction in the number of attempts to access the network, while improving the average sum-rate, as the number of SA increases.

articleTitle: A Cyber-Physical System for Energy Efficiency and Indoor Air Conditioning of Multiple Office Rooms
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems are becoming a great tool to solve numerous problems of thing to thing and thing to human interaction, especially in the cases where the thing handles only part of the solution parameters, which is the case of the air cooling split systems devices, that are able to handle just the air room temperature and not the relative humidity, the renovation, the filtration and the sanitization of the air. Additionally, the control of the available adjustable parameters of an air cooling split system device through its remote control also can not cope with all the situations that can happen in an office room, such as variable thermal load, represented by the number of people and running equipment in the room, external weather conditions and people movement and personal preferences, for instance. This article presents the initial implementation of a Proof of Concept of Cyber-Physical System Project carried out at Renato Archer Information Technology Center, that aims to improve comfort, health and safety for people in multiple office rooms equipped with air cooling split systems devices, taking into account energy efficiency constraints and innovatives man machine interaction. It is shown in this work the concepts, the hardware and the software frameworks used in the project, and some results, as well.

articleTitle: IoT Medical Device Architecture to Estimate Non-invasive Arterial Blood Pressure
abstract: High blood pressure (BP) is the leading cause of death worldwide. Besides being a treatable condition, alongside medication and a healthy diet, it requires regular BP measurements to assess whether a patient is properly responding to treatment. There have been many attempts to use the photoplethysmography (PPG) signal to estimate BP continuously, but there has yet to be an effective solution. This work presents our efforts to develop a new method for estimating BP from PPG and infrastructure to collect, process, and store this information. PPG signal is measured from a smartband; our App reads the data from the smartband to a smartphone, processes them using a machine learning method, and estimates BP, which is sent to a server that stores and displays the data.

articleTitle: Neuromorphic Hardware Applied in the Development of Low-Power IoTs *
abstract: In the field of study on smart cities, mapping information using Internet of Things (IoT) sensing is necessary because it allows optimizing resources through the real-time integration of the consumer with the supplier. However, world IoT production capacity would have to increase by two orders of magnitude to allow a meaningful level of mapping that could be felt in our daily lives. There are several technological challenges related to increasing IoT production by two orders of magnitude, such as the energy impact we would need to deal with. This work aims to introduce the idea that part of these challenges could be solved by changing the traditional computational architecture to the so-called Neuromorphic, a computational architecture based on biological brains. The work consisted of an extensive literature review that analyzed data on the specifications of prototypes of Neuromorphic architecture devices that were published in scientific databases. As a result, it was shown that Neuromorphic devices could meet the requirements and solve some challenges related to the increase that the world needs in the production of IoT, without the need for long periods of technology development.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an IoT-based Smart Charging Algorithm for Electric Vehicles Considering Multiprocessing
abstract: The worldwide adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) is a trend encouraged by sustainable policies that a growing number of countries are supporting. Consequently, the EV charging market players is a concept that is receiving particular attention, in which the charging station operator (CPO) is the player responsible for the infrastructure of the public EV charging stations (EVCSs). On the other hand, the integration of distributed energy resources (DER) and EVs within the electrical system requires the development of algorithms that allow CPOs to manage renewable energy sources aiming to serve EV charging. Internet of Things (IoT) makes it possible to develop an IoT platform that can help with the integration of a smart charging algorithm with the CPO. In this paper, a characterization of the IoT-middleware DOJOT platform (developed by the Brazilian research center CPqD) combined with two softwares developed under a Brazilian R&D project has been realized. The software under development aims to generate monthly policies for price variation and power limits for EVCSs and to perform smart charging of EVs considering DERs. Additionally, The evaluation was made through the performance of the DOJOT IoT platform and the software according to the number of devices that must be processed, internet connection quality, and multiprocessing.

articleTitle: LSTM-ACB-Based RA for IoT Mixed Traffic
abstract: A novel random access (RA) scheme for mixed URLLC-mMTC traffic scenario is proposed using realistic statistical models, with the use mode presenting long-term traffic regularity. The traffic is predicted by a long short-term memory neural network, which enables a traffic-aware resource slicing aided by contention access class barring-based procedure. The method combines a grant-free (GF) RA scheme with an intermediate step to congestion alleviation. The protocol trade-off is a small overhead while enabling a higher number of decoded received packets thanks to the intermediate step. Numerical results evaluate the system performance for each procedure and combined solution. A comparison with GF benchmark reveals substantial improvement in system performance.

articleTitle: RIS-aided System Channel Estimation using NN
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is an enabling technology to engineer the radio signal propagation in wireless networks. By smartly tuning the signal reflection via a large number of low-cost passive reflecting elements, RIS is capable of dynamically altering wireless channels to enhance the communication performance. Despite its great potential, RIS faces new challenges to be efficiently integrated into wireless networks, such as reflection optimization, channel estimation, and deployment from communication design perspectives. In this work, we propose a channel estimator for RIS-assisted systems based on machine learning techniques. We deploy a neural network (NN) with 3 fully connected hidden layers to provide RIS-aided channel estimation improvement using active and passive RIS elements.

articleTitle: Use of smart thermostat data to investigate harmful exposure to heat in Calgary, Canada
abstract: With the increase in temperatures and extreme heat events, developing a better strategy to assess and quantify heat exposure indoors is crucial. Although people spend most of their time indoors, most studies and alert systems focus on outdoor temperatures. The growing adoption of smart thermostats in home heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems offers an opportunity to study the relationship between indoor and outdoor temperatures. The present study uses indoor smart thermostats and weather station data to investigate heat exposure metrics for indoor and outdoor temperatures. We also analyzed the percentage of time indoor temperatures are within the ASHARE acceptability limit. We found that houses spend around 5% of the time above the ASHRAE limit and that indoor heat exposure metrics are higher than outdoor metrics, meaning greater harmful exposure to human health during extreme events like heatwaves.

articleTitle: Monitoring the Daily Rhythm of Total Green Leaf Volatiles with a Low-Cost Multi-Sensor Node
abstract: Plants emit volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from their leaves, flowers or fruits. These chemical signals have many functions ranging from hormonal regulation to complex interactions with pollinators and herbivores. Even diseases can influence the emission of VOCs. Thus, VOC monitoring might allow to deduce the abiotic and biotic stress of plants and to support data based decisions on countermeasures. However, most sensing methods for VOCs are not low-cost and mobile, which hinders widespread application. We report here on the possibility of employing off-the-shelf air quality sensors for sensing VOC levels emitted by plants. The developed low-cost multi-sensor node is described in detail. As a proof of principle, we monitor the VOC emission from the subshrub rue and show that a cyclic day-night rhythm of total VOC emission can be observed.

articleTitle: An Automated Workflow for Generation of Neural Networks for Embedded FPGAs on IoT
abstract: With the increasing popularity of artificial neural networks to solve a variety of issues for edge computing devices in the Internet of Things and the resource-intensive nature of these algorithms, there is a demand for hardware accelerators to optimize them. However, developing this type of device is usually locked behind specialized programming expertise and long design cycles. We propose an automatic generation workflow that, from a trained model, writes code for a hardware accelerator that optimizes the execution of the neural network that can be synthesizable in an FPGA. A proof of concept workflow with limited function compatibility was then created and an accelerator that is synthesizable in a small, low power FPGA is generated. It is then tested against a personal computer CPU, and significant speed up and energy efficiency gains are obtained.

articleTitle: A Low-cost IoT Mobile System for Monitoring Vital Signs of Elderly People
abstract: Elderly people need properly care in order to avoid falls and to have their vital signs monitored by family members or caregivers. Internet of Things (IoT) has a lot of products in the market to help the elderly. However, most of these products can only be acquired by upper class people. This paper proposes a low-cost trustful system for monitoring vital signs and providing basic life support for the elderly. The system consists of vital signs sensors coupled to a glove and a mobile app. The glove collects measurements of heart rate, blood oxygenation, environmental temperature, atmospheric pressure and detects whether the elderly person has fallen. The app shows the data collected by these measurements in real time. The system is based on the concept of Internet of Things (IoT) and uses the Firebase platform to store the data, presenting it in the mobile application. The proposed system present cheaper costs and equivalent measurements in relation to the market products.

articleTitle: JSGuide: A Tool to Improve JavaScript Algorithms Focusing on IoT Devices
abstract: JavaScript language (JS) was initially designed for browsers, but currently, it is applied to several contexts, such as server-side programming, mobile applications, games, robotics, and the Internet of Things (IoT). IoT devices are constrained in processing, memory, storage, and power consumption. Thus, developers need to consider their restrictions on embedded software development. However, to achieve great performance is necessary to have high knowledge about the programming language and device limitations, preferably without forgetting design-time qualities like readability, maintainability, and code reuse. This paper introduces JSGuide, a tool to produce guidelines focusing on embedded software for JavaScript language. We investigate which techniques or JS language aspects can enhance the application in performance, memory usage, security, and maintainability. The tool was developed in Java and performs static code analyses over embedded software for flaw detection. As a result, the software produces a report that points out all the points in the source code that can be reviewed. Our finding shows that the application can improve its performance if suggested modifications are applied.

articleTitle: Critical analysis of ITU-R P.1812 and Egli propagation models for LoRaWAN Networks
abstract: In the current scope of IoT, low power wide-area-networks represent a key subject. Currently, LoRa is one of the main technologies that drive the growing use of such networks. In the planning process to design any LPWAN such as a LoRaWAN network, it is essential to make a coverage study, taking into consideration the various aspects of the scenario of implementation, using, for that, an appropriate propagation model. This paper assesses two pertinent propagation models, the ITU-R P.1812 and Egli, comparing their performances in a rural area scenario, using field measurements. Good agreement between predictions and measurements was achieved with both models.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Sounding Rocket Telemetry System
abstract: Sounding rockets are essential for scientific and technological development. They are a relatively brief and not-so-expensive form of access to space. Rocket avionics is very complex and has many interfaces with ground crews before launch. Simplifying data exchange and making it more reliable and efficient is always very important. In this work, an IOT-based telemetry system for sounding rockets is proposed. Such architecture is expected to make data exchange and launch operation more efficient. The adaptations to achieve this goal are presented as well as the results of a proof of concept carried out with Heltec's LoRa 32 radio platform. The preliminary results of this work showed that an IoT-based telemetry can be used in sounding rocket projects, being able to successfully transmit and receive data.

articleTitle: Performance trade offs in IoT-based traffic monitoring and incident detection systems
abstract: Traffic monitoring systems are fundamental for making roads safer and more efficient. Newly proposed traffic monitoring systems enable the use of IoT devices to monitor traffic in a cost-effective way even over large distances on rural highways. These systems rely on machine learning algorithms which are too computationally expensive to run on the devices themselves, and so need to be executed in the cloud or over local processing nodes. In this work, we simulate an IoT-based traffic incident detection system deployed over a side road, comparing two different architectures: one with ad hoc communication and cloud processing, and the other based on edge computing. Results show that the networks based on edge computing have higher packet delivery rates in all scenarios and up to 30% faster round-trip time compared to the cloud-based approach.

articleTitle: Public Transportation Passengers Accounting at University by IoT Device
abstract: Public transport are alternatives for people daily locomotion due their economic and environmental factor, mainly in large cities. Acknowledgement about the vehicles use and people flux are mandatory to achieve better cost efficiency in the different modes of transport. In this scenario, a real-time people flux acquisition system make possible optimized planning and operation by identification of peak and daily demands. A good way to get such information is through automatic passenger counters associated with Global Navigation Satellite System which allows to geographical cross-reference the demand. This work describes the development and validation of the hardware and firmware of a low-cost Internet of Things solution for passengers boarding and alighting counting on buses from the internal public transportation system at the University of Campinas. The developed low cost device uses infrared sensors to detect people boarding/alighting and an ESP32 microcontroller to accumulate and send the data through Message Queue Telemetry Transport communication under GPRS wireless network.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces to Enable Energy-Efficient IoT Networks
abstract: In this article, we study the uplink (UL) channel of a cellular network of Internet of Things (IoT) devices assisted by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) with a limited number of reflecting angle configurations. Firstly, we derive an expression of the required transmit power for the machine-type devices (MTDs) to attain a target signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), considering a channel model that accounts for the RIS discretization into sub-wavelength reflecting elements. Such an expression demonstrates that the transmit power depends on the target SNR, the position of the MTD in the service area, and the RIS setup, which includes the number of reflecting elements and the available reflecting angle configurations. Secondly, we develop an expression for the expected battery lifetime (EBL) of the MTDs, which explicitly depends on the MTD transmit power. Numerical simulations on the energy efficiency (EE) evaluated via the EBL demonstrate the benefits of adopting RISs to enable energy-efficient IoT networks.

articleTitle: Optimizing Garbage Collection System
abstract: Garbage collection carried out improperly contributes to the impact on sustainability. Projections indicate that CO2 emissions related to solid waste will reach 2.38 billion tons/year by 2050. Waste collection is the first step of a management system, and its optimization with the help of IoT can reduce the impact. We model and prototype the waste collection management ecosystem that allows for efficient collection by monitoring garbage cans. The optimization in the route of the collection trucks indicated a gain of up to 20% in the resources involved.

articleTitle: Development of a Blockchain and IoT-based Platform for Animal Surveillance
abstract: Digital technologies such as Internet of Things are widely used in the veterinary area, including applications in animal health and welfare. The use of blockchain in this area is in the beginning, but many benefits may be achieved. This paper presents a proof of concept implementation of an animal surveillance system using blockchain and IoT. The architecture consists of a sensor-fog-cloud integration, including blockchain and smart contracts. The proof of concept used real horse temperature measurements, sending this data to a blockchain implemented with the Hyperledger Fabric platform. In the implementation and testing of the system, it was possible to observe that blockchain may improve the availability, immutability, security, and reliability of the data related to the application.
